title: Mitä: identifying a substance
focus: Use mitä with olla when asking what a substance is: Mitä tämä on? Mitä tämä on? — Tämä on vettä.
prerequisiteSkills: Mitä: asking and answering about actions and objects

exercises.prompt: Choose the question meaning “What is this?”  Ask about a substance.
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. The partitive is a word form used here for an amount, an action's object, or a substance or group description. Use mitä with olla when asking what a substance is: Mitä tämä on? (“What is this?” about an unidentified substance). This is why mikä with olla and mitä with other verbs is not a universal rule. The complete question means “What is this”.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: question asking a person's or thing's identity + subject (who or what this sentence is about) + verb (the action or state)

parts.role: question asking a person's or thing's identity
parts.formation: Mitä is the partitive form of mikä; its use follows the taught object or substance pattern.

parts.role: subject (who or what this sentence is about)
parts.formation: Tämä identifies one nearby person or thing; it stays in its basic form here.

parts.role: verb (the action or state)
parts.formation: Olla has the irregular singular third-person form on.

exercises.prompt: Answer “Mitä tämä on?”: choose “This is juice.”
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. Name the substance in the singular partitive: Tämä on vettä (“This is water”). A short reply Vettä is also natural. The question is about what the material is, not how much there is or what one countable object is. The complete reply means “This is juice”.
